subject.title: /think off doesn't disable thinking on claude-cli — inherits Claude Code's default effort (contradicts docs)

question: For `claude-cli`, should OpenClaw preserve host-managed Claude Code effort when users select `off`, coerce that selection to a documented minimum effort, or stop exposing `off` as a disable-thinking state when Claude Code cannot enforce it?
rationale: Claude Code’s effort flag has no documented `off` value in the evidence supplied, so selecting a fallback level or changing the offered user-facing state is an intentional provider-product contract rather than a mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Do not advertise unsupported disablement
options.body: Recommended: expose only Claude CLI thinking states with an enforceable outcome and update the UI/docs to distinguish host-managed adaptive effort from disabled thinking.

options.title: Treat off as low effort
options.body: Pass `--effort low` after removing any configured effort override, documenting that Claude CLI has a lowest-effort floor rather than true thinking disablement.

options.title: Keep inherited host defaults
options.body: Keep omission semantics but relabel the state as adaptive or inherited so it no longer claims to disable thinking.

recommendation.title: Do not advertise unsupported disablement
recommendation.body: Recommended: expose only Claude CLI thinking states with an enforceable outcome and update the UI/docs to distinguish host-managed adaptive effort from disabled thinking.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent provider-specific `/think off` work makes this the strongest available routing candidate, though exact ownership needs local-history confirmation.
